adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCache.handler.ts:12-18 - access check requires `userId: user.id` which blocks cache deletion for delegation/managed credentials (userId is null or a team id), while `CredentialActionsDropdown` still shows the 'Delete cached data' action, so users on managed calendars always get 'Error deleting cache'; correct scoping (e.g., delegation credential team membership) needs to be added

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown`, the cache action is shown whenever `integrationType === GOOGLE_CALENDAR_TYPE` and `cacheUpdatedAt` is truthy (`hasCache`), regardless of `delegationCredentialId` / `disableConnectionModification` (those only affect `canDisconnect`). However, `deleteCache.handler.ts` authorizes by requiring a `Credential` row with `id: credentialId` and `userId: user.id`. For delegation/managed credentials (explicitly treated specially elsewhere in the diff via `delegationCredentialId` and prior “can’t be disconnected” comments), this ownership check can fail, causing the mutation to throw and the UI to always show the error toast when users try “Delete cached data”. The diff therefore introduces a verifiable UI/server scoping mismatch for delegated credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: connectedCalendars.handler.ts:27-28 - `credentialId` may be null/undefined in the `connectedCalendars` list fed into `where: { credentialId: { in: [...] } }`, causing a Prisma validation error that turns the entire connected calendars page/endpoint into a 500 for affected users

adjudication.rationale: In `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`, the new code does `const credentialIds = connectedCalendars.map((cal) => cal.credentialId);` and passes that to `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` which uses `where: { credentialId: { in: credentialIds } }`. However, nothing in this diff shows that `connectedCalendars` can contain items with `credentialId` being `null`/`undefined`—the existing UI code already assumes `connectedCalendar.credentialId` is present (used as a `number` in multiple places), and the diff does not change the source/type of `connectedCalendars` to make `credentialId` optional. The finding asserts a nullability issue that is not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:26-31 - `deleteCacheMutation` only calls the caller's `onSuccess?.()` and never invalidates the `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` tRPC cache, leaving stale UI showing the old timestamp and 'Delete cached data' menu item after successful deletion

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx`, `deleteCacheMutation`’s `onSuccess` only shows a toast and calls `onSuccess?.()`; unlike `disconnectMutation`, it does not invalidate any tRPC/react-query caches (e.g. `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()`). Since the connected calendars list is enriched with `cacheUpdatedAt` in `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`, failing to invalidate/refetch after `deleteCache` can leave the UI showing a stale `cacheUpdatedAt` and the cache menu until some other refetch happens. The diff does not prove `onSuccess` always triggers a refetch, so the “stale UI” outcome is plausible but not strictly verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration 20250715160635 / schema.prisma - backfilling legacy `CalendarCache` rows with `updatedAt = NOW()` gives pre-existing cache entries a fresh-looking 'Last updated' timestamp despite arbitrarily old data, misleading users; no `expiresAt`-based backfill was attempted

adjudication.rationale: The migration adds `CalendarCache.updatedAt` as `NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()` (migration.sql) and schema sets `@default(now()) @updatedAt`, which will backfill all existing `CalendarCache` rows with the migration-time timestamp. The new UI/logic uses this field to display cache freshness: `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` returns `_max.updatedAt`, `connectedCalendars.handler` maps it to `cacheUpdatedAt`, and `CredentialActionsDropdown` shows `cache_last_updated` using that value. This means pre-existing cache entries will appear recently updated even if their underlying cached `value` is old, which is misleading and directly caused by the diff; no alternative backfill (e.g., derived from `expiresAt`) is present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCache.handler.ts - race window between `deleteMany` and concurrent re-population: endpoint returns success and UI shows 'deleted successfully' even though new rows may already exist

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts`, the mutation simply does `await prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } })` and then returns `{ success: true }` with the UI toast wired to `onSuccess`. There is no transactional guard, no cache "generation" token, and no post-condition check to ensure the cache remains empty after the call. If other parts of the system can repopulate the cache concurrently (not shown here, but suggested by other caching logic in the diff), the UI message may be misleading. However, the diff does not establish a concrete incorrectness/security issue—just an edge-case/semantics concern about what “deleted successfully” guarantees.

deleteCache bypasses `CalendarCacheRepository` - the handler calls `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany` directly instead of the existing `deleteManyByCredential` repository method, breaking the graceful-degradation abstraction for calendar-cache-disabled deployments

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts`, the handler deletes cache rows via `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } })` instead of using the calendar-cache repository abstraction. The diff shows there is an `ICalendarCacheRepository` with a `deleteManyByCredential` method and a `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` that intentionally no-ops when calendar-cache is disabled (logs “Skipping ... due to calendar-cache being disabled”). Bypassing the repository here creates an inconsistency with that graceful-degradation pattern and could undermine whatever “calendar-cache disabled” mode relies on the mock behavior, even though the diff alone doesn’t prove such a mode is active for this handler.

adjudication_records.issue_text: updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data object {} at CalendarService.ts:1023 / selectedCalendar.ts:400, causing Prisma validation error or a no-op, breaking the intended updatedAt bump and potentially failing the getAvailability cache-miss path

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `GoogleCalendarService` calling `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` (CalendarService.ts). The repository implementation simply forwards `data` into `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany({ where: { credentialId }, data })` (selectedCalendar.ts). Passing an empty `data` object to Prisma `updateMany` is typically invalid (Prisma expects at least one field in `data`) and, even if it were accepted, it would not bump `updatedAt` because no actual update is specified. This can therefore throw at runtime or be a no-op, defeating the stated intent to update `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCache ownership check uses userId: user.id, denying access to organization/delegation credentials (userId: null) that the UI shows the delete-cache action for, causing 'Credential not found or access denied' for credentials users legitimately use; should also permit org-scoped credentials

adjudication.rationale: The new `deleteCache` handler authorizes by `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })`, which will reject credentials not owned by the user (e.g., delegation/org-scoped credentials where `userId` may be `null` or different). Meanwhile, `CredentialActionsDropdown` shows the cache deletion action based only on `isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt` (`hasCache`) and explicitly allows the dropdown even when `canDisconnect` is false (e.g., `delegationCredentialId` present), so users can be offered “Delete cached data” for credentials that the backend will deny, resulting in the thrown "Credential not found or access denied".

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCacheHandler calls prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany directly, bypassing the CalendarCacheRepository abstraction and its mock used for deployments with calendar-cache disabled

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `deleteCacheHandler` directly calling `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } })` in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts`, while a `CalendarCacheRepository` abstraction exists (and its mock explicitly no-ops methods when calendar-cache is disabled in `calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts`). adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts:1022 — unconditional empty updateMany on every getAvailability call causes hot-path write amplification, issuing no-op UPDATEs for every SelectedCalendar row under the credential

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` in `CalendarService.ts` (commented as updating `updatedAt`). This is executed unconditionally after fetching/setting availability, and it passes an empty `data` object into Prisma `updateMany`. From the diff alone, this is at least an unnecessary write query on a hot path (write amplification), and it may also be invalid at runtime since Prisma `updateMany` typically requires at least one field in `data` (empty updates can throw).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Passing {} as Prisma update data either throws a Prisma validation error or is a silent no-op, so updatedAt is never actually bumped; the refresh should be explicit (e.g. new Date()) and only fire inside the cache-miss branch

adjudication.rationale: In `CalendarService.ts`, the new line `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` is intended to bump `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`, but it passes an empty Prisma `data` object. Prisma update/updateMany generally requires at least one field in `data` and can throw a validation error, and even if it didn’t, an empty update would be a no-op so `updatedAt` would not be reliably refreshed. Also, it is placed after the cache-miss conditional, so it will run on both cache hits and misses, contrary to the finding’s “only inside cache-miss branch” expectation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: connectedCalendars.handler.ts:27-32 — getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groupBy query may scan if no index covering credentialId + updatedAt exists on CalendarCache; verify or add such an index

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new Prisma `groupBy` on `calendarCache` in `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds()` (called from `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`) with `where: { credentialId: { in: credentialIds } }` and `_max: { updatedAt: true }`. This can become a performance issue if `CalendarCache` lacks a supporting index on `credentialId` (and potentially `updatedAt`) to efficiently compute the max per credential. The diff does not show any index additions, but it also doesn’t prove none exists already, so it’s a reasonable “verify/add index” review concern rather than a confirmed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data object won't bump updatedAt since SelectedCalendar.updatedAt lacks @updatedAt, causing the update to throw or be a silent no-op, breaking getAvailability or leaving stale cache status

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new call `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty `data` object. In `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId`, this is forwarded directly to `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany({ where: { credentialId }, data })`. Prisma `updateMany` requires at least one field in `data`; an empty object is likely to trigger a runtime validation error (or at best be a no-op), which can break the surrounding `getAvailability` flow. The part of the finding about `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` lacking `@updatedAt` is not verifiable from this diff, but the empty-update call itself is a concrete defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getAvailability performs an unconditional updateMany write against SelectedCalendar on every availability request, adding a DB write per read in the hot path; should be moved to cache refresh or throttled

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCache deletes CalendarCache rows but not SelectedCalendar.updatedAt markers, leaving inconsistent cache freshness state after user deletes cached data

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCache.handler.ts:24 throws a plain Error instead of a TRPCError (e.g., NOT_FOUND/UNAUTHORIZED), surfacing as untyped INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCache tRPC route (handler throws plain Error('Credential not found or access denied') instead of a typed TRPCError, conflating unauthorized vs not-found and yielding generic INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR) has no test asserting client-received error shape, and the client onError toast behavior in CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:36-38 is unverified

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration/schema default mismatch: migration.sql sets DB default to NOW() but Prisma @updatedAt only auto-updates via Prisma writes, so raw inserts get a misleading static timestamp, and no test verifies updatedAt is actually bumped on cache writes (setAvailabilityInCache path) — the feature's core cache-freshness signal is unproven

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally aligns DB and Prisma: migration adds `CalendarCache.updatedAt TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()`, and `schema.prisma` adds `updatedAt @default(now()) @updatedAt`, which is a common pattern (DB default for inserts/legacy rows; Prisma-managed bump on Prisma updates). The claim that this creates a “misleading static timestamp” for raw inserts is not supported: `NOW()` is evaluated at insert time and is correct for initial freshness. The assertion about `setAvailabilityInCache` not bumping `updatedAt` and missing tests is not verifiable from the diff because no cache-write logic/tests are shown here beyond adding the field and reading it via `groupBy`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:55 hardcodes isGoogleCalendar check, coupling a generic component to Google-specific logic; cache presence is already encoded in the data payload

This is a real, diff-grounded inconsistency that could mislead reviewers/operators, but it doesn’t affect runtime behavior since it’s only a comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: updateManyByCredentialId in CalendarService.ts:1023 passes an empty data object, so the 'cache updated' timestamp never updates — either a Prisma validation error or silent no-op, leaving SelectedCalendar.updatedAt stale and cache-status display meaningless

adjudication.rationale: In `CalendarService.ts` the new call `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` passes an empty `data` object into `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany({ ..., data })` (see `selectedCalendar.ts`). An empty update payload is likely invalid in Prisma (runtime validation error) or a no-op, so it would not accomplish the stated goal of bumping `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. Note: the PR’s cache-status UI is driven by `CalendarCache.updatedAt` (via `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`), not `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`, so the finding’s “cache-status display meaningless” rationale is not supported by the diff—but the empty update itself is still a real correctness risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCache.handler.ts ownership check `where: { id, userId: user.id }` fails for delegation/org credentials with userId: null, so users see the 'Delete cached data' button but always get 'Credential not found or access denied' with no org-admin fallback

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown`, the "Delete cached data" action is shown whenever `hasCache` is true (`isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt`), with no restriction based on `delegationCredentialId` or org/admin status. However, `deleteCache.handler.ts` authorizes strictly via `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })`. If a connected calendar credential is a delegation/org credential (the UI already treats these specially for disconnect via `delegationCredentialId`), it may not have `userId` matching the current user (possibly `null`), causing the handler to throw "Credential not found or access denied" even though the UI can present the delete-cache option.

adjudication_records.issue_text: connectedCalendars.handler.ts:29 instantiates CalendarCacheRepository directly instead of using the factory, bypassing the disabled-cache abstraction and potentially erroring in environments with calendar-cache disabled

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts` the new code imports and instantiates `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly, then calls `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`. The diff also shows a `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` whose methods log “Skipping … due to calendar-cache being disabled”, implying there is (or should be) an abstraction to swap implementations when cache is disabled. This handler does not use the interface/factory/injection path, so it can’t benefit from that swap and will always hit Prisma (`prisma.calendarCache.groupBy`). The claim that this will definitely error in disabled environments isn’t provable from the diff, but bypassing the intended abstraction is a concrete architecture/scope issue introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCacheMutation.onSuccess in CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, so UI shows stale cache status and delete option after deletion

adjudication.rationale: In CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx, deleteCacheMutation.onSuccess only shows a toast and calls onSuccess?.() and does not invalidate/refetch trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars (unlike disconnectMutation which explicitly invalidates connectedCalendars and integrations). The claim that the UI will definitely be stale can’t be proven from the diff because the parent’s onSuccess callback may trigger a refetch, but the lack of invalidation in this component is a concrete, diff-grounded issue that could lead to stale cacheUpdatedAt/delete option.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds filters only on credentialId and ignores expiresAt, so expired cache rows are reported as valid cache with a 'Last updated' timestamp

adjudication.rationale: `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups by `credentialId` and returns `_max.updatedAt` with a `where` clause that only filters on `credentialId` (`where: { credentialId: { in: credentialIds } }`) and does not consider `expiresAt`. The UI logic then treats any non-null `cacheUpdatedAt` as `hasCache` and shows “Cache Status”/“Last updated” (`hasCache = isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt`). If expired `CalendarCache` rows remain in the table, this will still report a cache timestamp even though the cache should be considered expired based on `expiresAt`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCache.handler.ts:27 throws raw Error instead of TRPCError with a code, giving the client an opaque 500 instead of NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts`, when the credential is not found/accessible the handler does `throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. In tRPC, throwing a raw `Error` typically maps to `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` (HTTP 500) rather than a specific `TRPCError` code like `NOT_FOUND` or `FORBIDDEN`, so the client can’t reliably distinguish expected auth/not-found conditions from real server failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:66 uses BSD/macOS-only `sed -i ''` which fails on GNU/Linux
matched_golden_ids: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly flags use of `sed -i ''` as BSD/macOS-only and notes it fails on GNU/Linux, which is the same cross-platform sed `-i` empty-string syntax issue described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx hard-codes en-US locale in Intl.DateTimeFormat instead of using the user's locale via i18n conventions

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx`, the timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" })`, which hard-codes the locale instead of using the user’s locale (even though `useLocale()` is available via `t`). This is a real i18n/UX concern introduced by the diff, but it’s not a functional correctness defect.
